data.narrative:
QunaSys is a Series B quantum computing company that has raised $33M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers—3 publicly traded (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ—though the private cohort lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage overlap for reliable peer-median benchmarking.

Given the narrow peer set at QunaSys's specific stage and valuation tier, only the stage-progression method was applicable. This approach uses the $33M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding an implied valuation of $63M. This represents the core quantitative anchor for the analysis.

The triangulated range derived from this single methodology is $53M (low), $63M (median), to $72M (high), reflecting reasonable sensitivity bounds around the stage-progression result. The primary uncertainty is the absence of tighter private peer comparables; while eight quantum computing companies exist in the broader dataset, none provided sufficient overlap on stage, valuation tier, and business model to anchor a peer-median cross-check. Public comps offer only indirect reference points given the heterogeneity of quantum hardware, software, and application approaches. Investors should treat the $53M–$72M range as a working estimate subject to material revision as the quantum computing sector matures and more comparable Series B transactions emerge.
